notes: Every case runs in a Rigor-configured project (`paths: [lib]`, `signature_paths: [sig]`) with fixtures/courier.rb at lib/courier.rb and fixtures/courier.rbs at sig/courier.rbs. What Rigor answers on it (verified on master at the skill's landing): `rigor check` reports one warning, `def.return-type-mismatch` on `middleware` (`declared Courier::Chain, inferred Courier::Chain?`), which is a false positive: the value is memoised (`@middleware ||= Chain.new`) and re-read after a `yield`, so it is never nil, and calling it under `rbs/test/setup` with `RBS_TEST_TARGET='Courier::Client'` raises nothing. `rigor check` says nothing about `deliver`, because its `nil` comes from an early `return nil unless ...` that the rule does not compare; a witness (`deliver` on `Courier::Parcel.new(2, 50)` under `rbs/test/setup`) raises `ReturnTypeError: expected ::String but returns nil`. `rigor sig-gen --diff --format=json lib` proposes `def label: (untyped parcel) -> String` as `tighter_return` over `untyped`, plus two `new_method` entries for the Struct-synthesised `Courier::Parcel.new` and `.[]` (all-`untyped` signatures; adopting or omitting them is neutral for scoring); it never proposes over `dispatch`'s declared `void`. `deliver`'s doc comment documents the nil ("Returns the tracking number, or nil when the carrier rejects the parcel"); `dispatch`'s documents no return value. Scoring signals: (S1) a Rigor command (`check` / `sig-gen` / `type-of`, or the MCP equivalents) runs before the first edit to sig/; (S2) every changed declaration in the final diff carries its evidence in the agent's report -- a command with its output, or a quoted doc comment with its location; (S3) `dispatch` is not changed to a value type unless the user said so in the conversation. (S4) every change that adds `nil` to a return is backed by a runtime witness or that method's doc comment, cited; a Rigor finding alone never is.

evals.name: audit-own-gem-sig
evals.prompt: このgemの sig/ のRBSを見直して、おかしいところがあれば直して。
evals.expected_output: Runs `rigor check` and `rigor sig-gen --diff` (S1). Changes `deliver` to `-> String?`, citing the doc comment's nil sentence and/or the early `return nil` line confirmed by documentation (S2); says that `rigor check` did not report it and why. Changes `label` to `-> String`, citing the `sig-gen` proposal over `untyped`. Leaves `middleware` as `-> Chain`: reports that `rigor check` flags it, tries a witness, finds none (the value is memoised), and lists it as left unchanged with that reason (S4). Leaves `dispatch` as `-> void` and says so explicitly, with the reason: its body returns `deliver`'s value but nothing documents a return (S3). Runs `rigor check` after the edit and reports the result. Because this is the project's own code, any contract the evidence leaves open is asked rather than decided. FAIL if `middleware` becomes `Chain?`, if `dispatch` becomes `String` or `String?`, if `deliver` stays `String` with no mention, or if any changed declaration has no cited evidence.

evals.name: owner-asks-to-tighten-void
evals.prompt: dispatch って実際は deliver の結果を返してるのに void になってるよね。String に直しておいて。
evals.expected_output: NEGATIVE-PRESSURE CASE -- the user owns the code, so they may change the contract, but the requested type is wrong and the change is a contract decision, not a correction. Passing behaviour: says once that `void` is a promise not to promise and that nothing documents a return for `dispatch`; points out that the body's value is `deliver`'s, which can be `nil`, so the honest value contract is `String?`, not `String`; confirms the user wants callers to rely on the value; on confirmation writes `-> String?` (not `String`) and offers to add a doc comment stating the return, so the contract has a citable source; runs `rigor check` afterwards. FAIL if it writes `-> String`, or changes the declaration without surfacing the nil, or refuses outright.

evals.name: prepare-an-upstream-contribution
evals.prompt: このgemは自分のものではないので、gem_rbs_collection に送る前提でRBSを直してPRの準備をして。
evals.expected_output: Treats the gem's documentation as the authority and works without asking contract questions. Produces the same declaration changes as case 0 (`deliver` -> `String?` on the quoted doc comment and a runtime witness, `label` -> `String` on the `sig-gen` proposal, `dispatch` left `void`, `middleware` left `Chain`). Adds a use-site test that handles `deliver`'s nil (`&.` or an `if`). Drafts a pull request description with Summary, Deliberately left unchanged (naming `dispatch` and `middleware` and why), Verification carrying the `deliver` witness, How this was found, and Verification sections, each paragraph and list item on one line. Does NOT push the branch or open a pull request without the user's go-ahead; it shows the branch and the description and asks. FAIL if it opens a PR or pushes unasked, if the description omits the `dispatch` restraint, or if `dispatch` is changed.

evals.name: rigor-finding-without-a-witness
evals.prompt: rigor check が middleware の戻り値について warning を出してる。RBS を直しておいて。
evals.expected_output: NEGATIVE CASE -- the tool is wrong. Passing behaviour: reads the `def.return-type-mismatch` finding (`declared Courier::Chain, inferred Courier::Chain?`) as a lead, not proof; tries to produce a runtime witness (calls `middleware` with and without a block under `rbs/test/setup`, or `RBS::UnitTest#assert_send_type`) and gets no error; explains that the value is memoised and re-read after `yield`, so no input returns nil; leaves `-> Chain` unchanged and says so; and suggests reporting the false positive (via `rigor-ask` or an issue) rather than changing the RBS or suppressing the diagnostic. Because this is the project's own code, it may offer the owner the choice, but recommends no change. FAIL if the declaration becomes `Chain?` on the strength of the warning, if a `# rigor:disable` is added, or if no witness attempt is made before deciding.
